laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences, even for possession of small amounts of recreational drugs or some prescription medications, include: heavy fines imprisonment being removed and banned from the Schengen area.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry an ID, such as your driver's licence or a copy of your passport. If you assault someone in any way, you may be jailed, deported and banned from the Schengen area. Alcohol laws are very strict, and penalties for driving under the influence are severe. The legal limit is 0.02% blood alcohol and applies to the driver of any motorised vehicle. There are frequent roadside drink driving checks. If you speed or drive under the influence: penalties are severe you may face jail or deportation you may be banned from the Schengen area.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Norway is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Svalbard isn't in Schengen; Schengen rules apply again on return to the mainland.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: Luftfartstilsynet (CAA Norway) publishes a list of registered drone operators. The Open category needs no authorisation; the Specific category needs one, and third-country operators apply to Norway (form NF-1145) if it is the first EASA state they fly in. Russian drone operators are banned.

register.name: CAA Norway: registered drone operators in Norway

items.text: CAA Norway lists registered operators under 'Registered operators in Norway'. The page read does not say what the list shows or how it is searched.

Flights that do not fit the Open category need an operational authorisation in the Specific category (with a risk assessment). Liability insurance is needed for Specific category operations. Registration, online courses and the exam are done at flydrone.no.

Operators from EASA member states first obtain authorisation at home, then send CAA Norway form NF-1154, the authorisation and proof of insurance. Operators based outside EASA states register and apply in the first EASA state where they plan to fly (for Norway, form NF-1145); processing and annual fees apply. If you can fly in the Open category, no authorisation is needed.

Visit Norway's image and video bank is searchable without an account; ordering needs registration, acceptance of the terms and a statement of intended use. The page does not mention aerial or drone footage. Material is free to use in articles that promote Norway as a travel destination, with the photographer and Visitnorway.com credited. Films download free in low resolution; the licence does not cover TV or cinema advertising. Clips tagged "stock video" may be edited.
